questions.stem: Consider this: A driver who struck a pedestrian is charged after the prosecution proves the act but not the state of mind. The statute defines the crime with a knowing requirement. Which statement best states the governing legal rule on these facts?

options.text: Any harmful outcome creates criminal liability regardless of how the defendant's body moved on these facts.
A decision to commit a crime is itself the criminal act even if nothing outward happens on these facts.
A movement is voluntary only if the defendant intended the resulting harm on these facts.

Each distractor rests on a different mistake about how the doctrine operates.
questions.hint: Separate the physical movement from the mental state. Keep the inquiry on the requirement of a voluntary act.
